title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Summary:
This document describes Redwood Inference's standard processes and templates for hiring, employee onboarding, performance and feedback cycles, and manager responsibilities. It is intended as the single-source-of-truth for people-ops and managers to run consistent, compliant, and coaching-focused people programs.

1. Introduction
A short summary of intent and scope:
- Audience: hiring managers, interviewers, people-ops partners, HRBP, new hires, and engineering managers.
- Scope: full lifecycle from requisition -> hire -> 30/60/90 onboarding -> ongoing performance management -> offboarding.
- Owner: People Operations (people-ops@redwood.ai).

2. Hiring process (end-to-end)
Overview: structured, bias-reducing, and speed-conscious. Key goals: time-to-offer <= 30 days for IC roles, quality-of-hire measured by hiring manager satisfaction and first-year retention.

2.1 Requisition & approval
- Manager creates a requisition in Workday (HRIS). Include role spec, salary band, and preferred internal referral.
- People-ops reviews headcount budget and confirms EEs (salary band, level).
- Approvals: Manager -> Director -> Finance (for net new FTE) -> People-ops.
- SLA: approvals within 5 business days.

2.2 Sourcing and outreach
- Sourcing channels: employee referrals, LinkedIn Recruiter, GitHub, community events, university programs, external agency (approved list).
- Diversity step: ensure slate includes at least one underrepresented candidate for senior roles where feasible.

2.3 Interview loop and scorecard
- Standard loop (IC engineering role): Recruiter screen (30m) -> Hiring manager screen (30m) -> Technical exercise (take-home or live depending on level) -> Onsite loop (3-4 interviews, 45-60m each) -> Debrief.
- Interviewers must use the role-specific scorecard and submit feedback in Greenhouse within 24 hours.

Scorecard template (use in Greenhouse notes):
| Dimension | Rating (1-5) | Evidence / Notes | Strengths | Risks |
|-----------|-------------:|------------------|----------|-------|
| Technical skills | | | | |
| System design / architecture | | | | |
| Problem solving | | | | |
| Communication & collaboration | | | | |
| Role fit & ownership | | | | |

2.4 Decision & offer
- Debrief meeting within 48 hours of onsite. Hiring manager drives decision.
- People-ops generates offer packet: base, bonus/eq guidance, benefits summary, start date, relocation policy (if applicable).
- Typical target: make offer within 7 business days of final interview.

2.5 Background checks & I-9
- People-ops initiates background and employment eligibility checks immediately after offer acceptance.
- Candidate must complete I-9 within their first week; work with People-ops for remote verification options.

3. Onboarding (first 90 days)
Objective: accelerate impact and retention by providing structure, systems access, and social integration.

3.1 Pre-boarding (0-7 days before start)
- People-ops actions: send welcome email, benefits enrollment instructions, and company handbook link.
- IT actions: create Okta account, request laptop order, grant base GCP/AWS project access, Slack invite, Confluence access.
- Manager actions: schedule first-week calendar (meet & greets, team orientation, 1:1 cadence).

3.2 First day checklist
- HR: benefits overview, payroll setup, policy review (code of conduct, security).
- Manager: team lunch (virtual or in-person), 1:1 to review role expectations and 30/60/90 plan.
- New hire: complete required security training modules in LMS.

3.3 30/60/90 day plan (manager + new hire)
- 30-day goals: onboard to codebase, complete mandatory trainings, ship first small bug or documentation improvement.
- 60-day goals: own a small feature, cross-team introduction, present a learnings summary.
- 90-day goals: take on full scope of role responsibilities, set long-term objectives with manager (career path discussion).

3.4 Access provisioning table (minimum required)
| System | Access owner | Standard access level | Notes |
|--------|--------------|-----------------------|-------|
| Okta | IT Ops | Employee | SSO for all SaaS apps |
| GitHub | Eng Platform | Contributor | Repo-level permissions set by team lead |
| GCP / AWS | Cloud Infra | Project viewer/editor | Grant via IAM request form |
| Slack | IT Ops | Member | Channel onboarding: #team, #engineering, #announcements |
| Confluence | Docs | Editor | Team spaces added by doc owner |

3.5 Training & mentorship
- Mandatory trainings: security, privacy, code review standards, company values.
- Assign a buddy for first 90 days. Schedule weekly syncs for first month.

4. Performance & feedback cycles
Philosophy: continuous feedback with structured checkpoints. Emphasize development, calibration, and fair assessments.

4.1 Cadence
- Quarterly check-ins: informal in-depth 1:1 with manager (documented).
- Formal performance cycle: annual review + mid-year calibration. Cycle dates: review window opens first week of November; calibration panels run mid-November.
- Probation/Onboarding review: 30/60/90-day manager check-ins documented in HRIS.

4.2 Rating scale & calibration
- Rating scale: 1 (Needs Improvement), 2 (Contributes), 3 (Exceeds), 4 (Outstanding). Managers must provide behavioral evidence for each rating.
- Calibration: managers present written evidence and sample work. People-ops facilitates cross-functional calibration panels to ensure consistency.

4.3 Career conversations & promotions
- Promotion packet: written summary, manager recommendation, sample work, peer feedback, and calibration outcome. Submit to People-ops and compensation for review. Typical promotion timelines: minimum 12 months in role unless exceptional.

4.4 Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)
- Trigger conditions: repeated failures to meet agreed goals after coaching and documented 1:1s.
- PIP components: clear objectives (SMART), success metrics, weekly check-ins, timeline (typically 60-90 days), HRBP involvement.
- Off-ramps: success (plan closed), extension (if clear progress), termination (if insufficient improvement).

5. Manager playbook (key responsibilities)
- Recruiting: craft role profile, participate in interviews, drive hiring decisions.
- Onboarding: prepare 30/60/90, schedule knowledge transfer, assign buddy.
- People development: run weekly/biweekly 1:1s, calibrate performance, approve development plans and training budgets (up to $1,200/yr per employee through L&D).
- Culture & inclusion: run inclusive interviews, discourage closed questions, provide accommodations as requested.
- Offboarding & escalation: follow offboarding checklist (revoke access, knowledge transfer, exit interview). Notify IT and People-ops at least one business day before last day.

6.1 Offer letter checklist
- Salary band, base salary, equity grant (if any), target bonus, start date, relocation details, key contacts (people-ops, manager, IT).

7. Offboarding checklist
- Manager: initiate offboarding ticket in HRIS, schedule knowledge transfer, notify team.
- IT: disable Okta, revoke VPN and cloud access on last working day, reclaim hardware.
- People-ops: conduct exit interview and close benefits.

8. Metrics & reporting
- Core metrics tracked monthly: time-to-fill, time-to-offer, acceptance rate, 12-month retention, hiring manager satisfaction (post-hire survey), diversity slate ratio.
- Owner: People-ops Analytics. Dashboards available in Looker: HR/Hiring Overview (link placeholder).

9. Escalations & exceptions
- For compensation or salary band exceptions: Manager -> Director of Engineering -> Head of People-ops -> CFO approval required. Document exceptions in People-ops ticket.
- For sensitive hires (security, government contractors, export-controlled): consult Security & Compliance team before offer.

10. Related policies & resources
- Company Handbook (benefits, PTO, code of conduct): confluence/company-handbook/employee-handbook-2025.json (link placeholder).
- Security onboarding & required trainings: confluence/security-and-compliance/onboarding-security-training-2025.json.
- Learning & development reimbursement policy: confluence/company-handbook/learning-and-development-policy-2025.json.

Appendix A: Quick-check templates
- First-week manager 1:1 agenda:

  2. Review 30/60/90 expectations (10m)
  3. Immediate blockers & resources needed (10m)
  4. Logistics: calendar, tools, access (5m)
  5. Next steps & follow-ups (5m)
